title: How to Create and Sell an Online Course in India
seoTitle: Create and Sell an Online Course in India | CloverLoop
description: Plan an online course in India from learner problem and curriculum to pricing, launch, delivery, refunds and course-support workflows.
primaryKeyword: create and sell online course India
imageAlt: Course creation and online learning ideas

blocks.text: An online course is more than a collection of recorded videos. A good course takes a learner from a starting point to a defined outcome through an ordered set of lessons, practice and feedback. The creator’s job is to make the learning path clear and to remove avoidable friction between purchase and progress.
Choose the right course outcome

Avoid broad promises such as “Master digital marketing” or “Become a professional guitarist”. A learner should be able to understand what they will be able to do after completing the course. A better promise is specific: “Build and publish your first portfolio website in four guided modules” or “Play five common rhythm patterns at a steady tempo using a 20-minute daily practice routine.”
Validate demand before recording everything

List the questions your audience asks repeatedly.
Offer a short live workshop or paid pilot covering one part of the outcome.
Observe where learners get stuck and which explanations they need repeated.
Use the pilot to design the course sequence, exercises and support requirements.
Record the full course only after you understand the learner’s actual difficulties.

blocks.text: How long should lessons be?

There is no ideal video length for every subject. Keep each lesson focused on one learning objective. A demonstration may need 12 minutes; a complex explanation may need 25. Split a lesson when the topic changes or when the learner needs a natural practice break. Do not cut a useful explanation merely to hit an arbitrary duration.
Choose a course delivery model
Recorded self-paced course

Learners buy access and study on their own schedule. This is easier to scale, but completion can be low if there is no structure or accountability. Provide a roadmap, suggested weekly schedule, downloadable practice material and clear support boundaries.
Live cohort course

Learners join a group that progresses together through scheduled sessions. Live interaction can improve accountability and allow questions, but the creator must manage scheduling, attendance, recordings, rescheduling and group support. Be explicit about session dates, time zone, recording availability and what happens if a learner misses a session.
Hybrid course

A hybrid course combines recorded lessons with live Q&A, feedback or office hours. This can balance repeatable teaching with human support. Price it based on the additional time commitment, not just the number of videos.
What platform features matter?

A clear course outline and lesson navigation.
Video playback that works on mobile networks and common devices.
Progress tracking or a clear way to resume learning.
Secure access controls and a defined access period.
Downloadable worksheets and supplementary resources.
A reliable checkout, payment confirmation and enrolment process.
A support channel and clear refund, cancellation and rescheduling policy.

blocks.text: How to price a course

Course pricing should reflect the outcome, learner support, depth, credibility and alternatives. A self-paced mini-course with no individual feedback should not be priced as if it includes personal coaching. Conversely, a cohort programme with live sessions, assignments and expert review requires time from the creator and should account for that delivery cost.

Use a simple capacity check. If a cohort has 20 learners and each learner receives 15 minutes of individual feedback, that is five hours of feedback time, before teaching, preparation and administration. If you price the course without accounting for this work, the creator may become overwhelmed as enrolments increase.

blocks.text: Protect the learner’s expectations

The sales page should state the exact syllabus, course format, instructor, prerequisites, software/equipment required, course duration, access period, live session dates, support limits, certificate status and refund policy. Do not imply that a certificate is government-recognised or professionally accredited unless that is true and documented.
Frequently asked questions
Can I sell a recorded course without live classes?

Yes. A recorded self-paced course can work well when the subject can be taught through structured lessons and practice material. The course should still provide a clear roadmap, examples, exercises and a way to resolve access or content questions. Consider adding a short FAQ or troubleshooting section to reduce repetitive support requests.
Do I need a separate website for my course?

No. You can use a hosted course platform, a creator storefront or your own website. Choose based on the learner experience you need: lesson navigation, video hosting, progress tracking, access controls, live sessions and downloadable resources. A simple payment link plus shared video folder may work for a small pilot but is not a robust long-term learning environment.
Should I issue a certificate?

You may issue a certificate of completion if you can define what completion means, such as watching required modules or submitting a project. Do not describe it as an accredited qualification unless the course is delivered through an appropriately recognised or approved institution or programme. A certificate designed by the creator is not automatically a government-recognised credential.
What should my refund policy say?

Explain the refund window, how a buyer requests a refund, what happens after course access is used, how live cohort cancellations are handled and whether missed sessions are refundable. The policy must comply with applicable consumer law and cannot remove rights that the law gives a buyer. Make the terms visible before payment.
